summary: An eight-minute peer check-in, called mainly so Michael could test Zoom on the internet at a short-let he had just moved into before taking a live sales call. The connection fails repeatedly and he ends up hotspotting from a phone with limited data. Richard gives a quick account of his day — one prospect disqualified for having no money, one no-show, and a long-standing lead who is a surgeon and has now cancelled on two different closers by being pulled into emergencies. They agree a mock call for the following day and end.
notable: A REP ASSERTED THAT NO-SHOW RATES TRACK WITH ETHNIC NAMES, APPLIED TO A NAMED BOOKED PROSPECT — Michael's next call was with a prospect called Abdul, and Richard responded: 'I do have to say it is just facts. No show rates with different names definitely do change. That is the facts... just people that are, like, called Abdul or something. I don't have anything against anyone. Like, I like anyone, right? But, like, always a no-sure rate with those names. We're always higher.' Michael did not challenge it and moved straight to confirming the call.

A CLOSER TOOK LIVE SALES CALLS ON A CONNECTION THAT COULD NOT LOAD A WEB PAGE — 'Dude, I can't even load another website. It's crazy', resolved only by hotspotting: 'I don't have unlimited data on my phone. So I'm gonna have to figure something out.' He had booked the accommodation last-minute and not verified the connection: 'on the listing it said the internet was good, but maybe I didn't go in as in-depth as I should have.' Any recording quality or dropout in this rep's calls from this period should be read against that.

A HIGH-VALUE LEAD HAS NOW CANCELLED ON TWO SEPARATE CLOSERS — 'a guy that has been in our system for like six months already. So I know when he jumps on, I'm going to close him. But getting him to jump on is going to be the difficulty, I think, because he's like in an operating room. So a couple of months ago, we canceled on a closer... Guess what he just did with me for the same reason.' A working surgeon is being repeatedly booked into slots he cannot attend.

Confirmation practice is manual and ad hoc: 'I got to text him and confirm. I probably should have called him', with Richard advising 'give him a call, just even if it's 30 minutes beforehand.' This matches the team-meeting instruction that closers confirm their own calls while the automated confirmer was misbehaving.
Richard reports disqualifying a prospect on the spot for having no money, alongside one no-show, as his day's outcome.
The Letting Go audiobook continues to circulate through the team as a shared performance practice: 'started listening to the book. It's working, it's helping, and letting go.'
